claim: Vibrio parahaemolyticus is a bacterial pathogen of humans and shrimp.
source: We take advantage of the unique population structure of Vibrio parahaemolyticus, a bacterial pathogen of humans and shrimp, to perform a genome-wide screen for coadapted genetic elements.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as established background information about the organism.

claim: 90 interaction groups (IGs) involving 1,560 coding genes were identified in Vibrio parahaemolyticus.
source: We identified 90 interaction groups (IGs) involving 1,560 coding genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding directly stated in the abstract and supported by the genome-wide screen performed.

claim: 82 interaction groups are between accessory genes in Vibrio parahaemolyticus.
source: 82 IGs are between accessory genes, many of which have functions related to carbohydrate transport and metabolism.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the coadaptation screen reported in the abstract.

claim: Many interaction groups between accessory genes have functions related to carbohydrate transport and metabolism.
source: 82 IGs are between accessory genes, many of which have functions related to carbohydrate transport and metabolism.
evidence: This is a functional characterization of the identified interaction groups based on data analysis.

claim: Only 8 interaction groups involve both core and accessory genomes.
source: Only 8 involve both core and accessory genomes.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the coadaptation screen stated in the abstract.

claim: The largest interaction group includes 1,540 SNPs in 82 genes and 338 accessory genome elements.
source: The largest includes 1,540 SNPs in 82 genes and 338 accessory genome elements, many involved in lateral flagella and cell wall biogenesis.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about the largest interaction group from the data analysis.

claim: Many elements in the largest interaction group are involved in lateral flagella and cell wall biogenesis.
source: The largest includes 1,540 SNPs in 82 genes and 338 accessory genome elements, many involved in lateral flagella and cell wall biogenesis.
evidence: This is a functional characterization of the largest interaction group based on gene annotation.

claim: The interactions have a complex hierarchical structure encoding at least four distinct ecological strategies.
source: The interactions have a complex hierarchical structure encoding at least four distinct ecological strategies.
evidence: This is a primary finding from hierarchical clustering analysis stated in the abstract.

claim: One ecological strategy involves a divergent profile in multiple genome regions.
source: One strategy involves a divergent profile in multiple genome regions, while the others involve fewer genes and are more plastic.
evidence: This characterizes one of the ecological strategies identified from the data analysis.

claim: Other ecological strategies involve fewer genes and are more plastic.
source: One strategy involves a divergent profile in multiple genome regions, while the others involve fewer genes and are more plastic.
evidence: This characterizes the other ecological strategies identified from the data analysis.

claim: Most genetic alliances are ephemeral.
source: Our results imply that most genetic alliances are ephemeral but that increasingly complex strategies can evolve and eventually cause speciation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results stated in the abstract.

claim: Increasingly complex strategies can evolve and eventually cause speciation.
source: Our results imply that most genetic alliances are ephemeral but that increasingly complex strategies can evolve and eventually cause speciation.
evidence: This is an interpretation and speculation about evolutionary implications based on the results.

claim: Complex phenotypic innovation requires adaptation at multiple genes.
source: As Darwin's argument implies, complex phenotypic innovation require adaptation at multiple genes and it is inevitable that some of the changes involved will be costly on the original genetic background, implying epistasis - that is non-additive fitness interactions - between adaptive loci.
evidence: This is stated as an established principle in evolutionary biology, drawing on Darwin's work.

claim: Some changes involved in complex phenotypic innovation will be costly on the original genetic background, implying epistasis between adaptive loci.
source: As Darwin's argument implies, complex phenotypic innovation require adaptation at multiple genes and it is inevitable that some of the changes involved will be costly on the original genetic background, implying epistasis - that is non-additive fitness interactions - between adaptive loci.
evidence: This is a logical inference from evolutionary theory about the nature of adaptation.

claim: In outbreeding animals, mating mixes up variation every generation.
source: For example, in outbreeding animals, mating mixes up variation every generation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about transmission genetics in outbreeding animals.

claim: Genes only increase in frequency if they have high average fitness across genetic backgrounds in outbreeding animals.
source: A consequence of continuous reassortment is that genes only increase in frequency if they have high average fitness across genetic backgrounds (Neher and Shraiman, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Neher and Shraiman, 2011.

claim: Extensive linkage disequilibrium due to natural selection is rare in outbreeding animals.
source: As a result, extensive linkage disequilibrium (LD) due to natural selection is rare (Pritchard and Przeworski, 2001)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Pritchard and Przeworski, 2001.

claim: Vibrio parahaemolyticus is capable of replicating in less than 10 min in appropriate conditions.
source: It is capable of replicating in less than 10 min in appropriate conditions (Makino et al., 2003)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Makino et al., 2003.

claim: The doubling time in the wild of Vibrio cholerae has been estimated as slightly over an hour.
source: while the doubling time in the wild of the related bacteria Vibrio cholerae has been estimated as slightly over an hour (Gibson et al., 1880).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Gibson et al., 1880.

claim: Approximately 0.017% of the Vibrio parahaemolyticus genome recombines each year.
source: Approximately 0.017% of the genome recombines each year (Yang et al., 2019a)
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2019a.

claim: There are approximately 50 million generations on average between recombination events at a given genetic locus in Vibrio parahaemolyticus.
source: implying that there are approximately 50 million generations on average between recombination events at a given genetic locus.
evidence: This is calculated based on the recombination rate and generation time data.

claim: The Asian population of V. parahaemolyticus has had a large effective population size for at least the last 15,000 years.
source: Although recombination happens slowly on the timescale of bacterial generations, the Asian population of V. parahaemolyticus has had a large effective population size for at least the last 15,000 years, or approximately 130 million bacterial generations (Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2018.

claim: There is approximate linkage equilibrium between most loci greater than 3 kb apart on the chromosome in V. parahaemolyticus.
source: As a result, the population of V. parahaemolyticus is unusual amongst bacteria in that there is approximate linkage equilibrium between most loci greater than 3 kb apart on the chromosome (Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2018.

claim: More than 14 billion Fisher exact tests were performed between variants in the core and accessory genomes.
source: We performed more than 14 billion Fisher exact tests between variants in the core and accessory genomes, using a cut-off of P < 10-10 with the aim of assembling a comprehensive list of common genetic variants that have strong LD between them due to fitness interactions.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: A cut-off of P < 10-10 was used to identify genetic variants with strong linkage disequilibrium.
source: We performed more than 14 billion Fisher exact tests between variants in the core and accessory genomes, using a cut-off of P < 10-10 with the aim of assembling a comprehensive list of common genetic variants that have strong LD between them due to fitness interactions.
evidence: This describes the statistical threshold used in the methodology.

claim: A non-redundant set of 469 genomes was generated by removing closely related strains that differed by less than 2,000 SNPs.
source: To minimize the effect of population structure we first removed closely related strains within our global collection of 1,103 isolates (Yang et al., 2019a) to generate a non-redundant set of 469 genomes that each differed from each other by more than 2,000 SNPs (Figure 1a).
evidence: This describes the data filtering methodology used in the study.

claim: The sample is subdivided into four distinct populations with different geographical distributions.
source: As previously described, the sample is subdivided into four distinct populations, which have different, although currently overlapping, geographical distributions (Yang et al., 2019a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Yang et al., 2019a and describes population structure.

claim: The discovery dataset consists of 198 strains from the Asian population.
source: We then used fineSTRUCTURE (Lawson et al., 2012) to look for signals of clonal structure within the remaining isolates, iteratively removing isolates until all of the isolates were assigned to a single population (Materials and methods), leading to a discovery dataset of 198 strains (Figure 1c, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the final discovery dataset used for the main analysis.

claim: 452,849 interactions with P < 10-10 were identified after excluding associations spanning less than 3 kb.
source: In order to exclude associations that arise only due to physical linkage, we excluded all sets of associations that spanned less than 3 kb, including between accessory genome elements. This left us with 452,849 interactions with P < 10-10
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the statistical analysis.

claim: The 452,849 interactions grouped into 90 interaction groups.
source: This left us with 452,849 interactions with P < 10-10, which grouped into 90 interaction groups (IG, a set of SNP/accessory gene connected by at least one significant interaction)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from clustering the interactions.

claim: All 90 interaction groups involved at least one accessory-genome element.
source: which grouped into 90 interaction groups (IG, a set of SNP/accessory gene connected by at least one significant interaction), all of which involved at least one accessory-genome element

claim: 35 interaction groups included multiple genome regions.
source: with 8 also including core genome SNPs and 35 including multiple genome regions.

claim: The interaction groups included 1,873 SNPs in 100 core genes and 1,460 accessory genome elements.
source: In total these IGs included 1,873 SNPs in 100 core genes and 1,460 accessory genome elements (Table 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of the genetic variants in interaction groups.

claim: Interacting SNPs were enriched for non-synonymous variants (26% vs. 16%, P < 0.01).
source: Interacting SNPs were enriched for non-synonymous variants (26% vs. 16%, P < 0.01, Fisher exact test), which is consistent with natural selection being the force generating the linkage disequilibrium we detected.
evidence: This is a statistical finding with a p-value from Fisher exact test.

claim: The enrichment of non-synonymous variants is consistent with natural selection generating the linkage disequilibrium.
source: Interacting SNPs were enriched for non-synonymous variants (26% vs. 16%, P < 0.01, Fisher exact test), which is consistent with natural selection being the force generating the linkage disequilibrium we detected.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the non-synonymous enrichment data.

claim: IG1 accounted for 82% of interacting SNPs.
source: The largest interaction group 1 (IG1) accounted for the majority of interacting SNPs (82%)
evidence: This is a quantitative characterization of IG1 from the data.

claim: IG1 accounted for 23% of accessory genome elements.
source: The largest interaction group 1 (IG1) accounted for the majority of interacting SNPs (82%) as well as a significant fraction of accessory genome elements (23%)
evidence: This is a quantitative characterization of IG1 from the data.

claim: IG2-IG90 generally consisted of a small number of interacting SNPs (0-297) and accessory genes (2-128).
source: while IG2-IG90 generally consisted of a small number of interacting SNPs (0-297) and accessory genes (2-128).

source: However, hierarchical clustering revealed that strains fall into four distinct 'ecogroups' (EGs) based on IG1 variants (Figure 3a,b).

claim: Three ecogroups (EG1a, EG1b and EG1d) have a large number of variants (50-965) associated with them.
source: Three of these groups, EG1a, EG1b and EG1d have a large number of variants (50-965) that are associated with them

claim: Within IG1, genes of COG classes M and N are substantially overrepresented relative to their overall frequency in the genome.
source: Within IG1, genes of COG classes M and N, cell wall biosynthesis and cell motility, are substantially overrepresented, relative to their overall frequency in the genome (COG M 32% vs 8%, COG N 13% vs 3%, P<0.01, Fisher exact test).

claim: 27% of the IG1 SNPs localize to the lateral flagella gene cluster.
source: 27% (509/1879) of the IG1 SNPs localize to the lateral flagella gene cluster (VPA1538-VPA1557).

claim: EG1a strains are highly diverged compared to other EGs in the number of core SNPs (831 SNPs in 47 genes) and accessory genes (134 genes).
source: EG1a strains are highly diverged compared to other EGs in the number of core SNPs (831 SNPs in 47 genes) and accessory genes (134 genes)

claim: EG1a strains revealed faster growth rate than EG1b-d strains.
source: However, EG1a strains revealed faster growth rate and significantly higher biofilm formation ability than EG1b-d strains (Figure 4b,c)

claim: EG1a strains revealed significantly higher biofilm formation ability than EG1b-d strains.
source: However, EG1a strains revealed faster growth rate and significantly higher biofilm formation ability than EG1b-d strains (Figure 4b,c)

source: Second, distinguishing direct associations – either through gene function or ecology – from those that arise due to mutual correlation with other interacting genes, is a substantial, and largely unaddressed challenge.
evidence: This is a statement about methodological challenges in the field.

claim: For the complex interaction groups, ARACNE criteria still left far too many interactions to be interpreted usefully as being causal.
source: For the complex interaction groups in our data, the criteria used by ARACNE (Margolin et al., 2006) to remove interactions still left far too many interactions to be interpreted usefully as being causal.
evidence: This is a finding about the limitations of ARACNE filtering.

claim: Hierarchical clustering organized the interactions in a manner that allowed informal interpretation.
source: We found that hierarchical clustering organized the interactions in a manner that allowed informal interpretation, but once again new statistical methodology is needed to facilitate detailed dissection of associations.
evidence: This is a finding about the utility of hierarchical clustering.

claim: Natural selection has a central role in determining accessory genome composition.
source: Using the same statistical threshold to assess significance, our interaction screen identifies many more examples of coadaptation between different accessory genome elements than of interactions between the core and accessory genomes or within the core genome, implying that natural selection has a central role in determining accessory genome composition.
evidence: This is an inference from the relative frequencies of different interaction types.

claim: The most common form of adaptation detected is the coinheritance of accessory genome elements located in the same region of the genome.
source: Unsurprisingly, given the extensive literature highlighting the importance of genomic islands to functional diversity of bacteria (Dobrindt et al., 2004), the most common form of adaptation detected by our screen is the coinheritance of accessory genome elements located in the same region of the genome.
evidence: This is a finding from the interaction screen with citation to relevant literature.

claim: The rarity of interactions between core and accessory genome reflects the evolution of 'plug and play'-like architecture for frequently transferred genetic elements.
source: We propose that the rarity of interactions between core and accessory genome in our scan reflects the evolution of 'plug and play'-like architecture for frequently transferred genetic elements.
evidence: This is a proposed explanation for the observed pattern.

claim: Accessory genome elements are more likely to establish themselves in new host genomes if they are functional immediately on arrival in a diversity of genetic backgrounds.
source: Accessory genome elements are more likely to establish themselves in new host genomes if they are functional immediately on arrival in a diversity of genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This is a theoretical argument about selection on accessory elements.

claim: From the host bacteria's point of view, acquisition of essential functions in new environments is more likely if diverse accessory genome elements in the gene pool are functional as soon as they are acquired.
source: Furthermore, from the point of view of the host bacteria, acquisition of essential functions in new environments is more likely if diverse accessory genome elements in the gene pool are functional as soon as they are acquired.
evidence: This is a theoretical argument about selection from the host perspective.

claim: Selection pressures will tend to promote a genomic architecture that facilitates casual gain and loss of genetic elements from particular genomes.
source: These selection pressures will tend to promote a genomic architecture that facilitates casual gain and loss of genetic elements from particular genomes (Figure 8a).
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion about evolutionary outcomes shown in Figure 8a.

claim: When an accessory genome element with an important protein coding function arrives in a new genome, optimization of gene regulation coordinating expression with others in the genome is likely possible.
source: When an accessory genome element with an important protein coding function arrives in a new genome, it is likely that some optimization of gene regulation will be possible, coordinating the expression of the gene with others in the genome.
evidence: This is a theoretical argument about regulatory evolution.

claim: Optimization of gene regulation can lead to longer-lasting associations between genetic elements.
source: This can lead to longer-lasting associations between genetic elements (Figure 8b).
evidence: This is a theoretical conclusion shown in Figure 8b.

claim: 8 different interaction groups involve core and accessory genome regions.
source: We found 8 different interaction groups involving core and accessory genome regions.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the interaction screen.

claim: Where coadaptation involves two or more separate genome regions, assembling fit combinations is more difficult.
source: Where coadaptation involves two or more separate genome regions, this makes assembling fit combinations more difficult and is likely to slow down the rate at which strains gain and lose the accessory genome elements involved.
evidence: This is a theoretical argument about the consequences of multi-locus coadaptation.

claim: The difficulty of evolving a trait de novo is likely to slow down the rate at which it is gained and loss.
source: The difficulty of evolving the trait de novo is likely to slow down the rate at which it is gained and loss, which in turn makes further coadaptation at additional genes more likely.
evidence: This is a theoretical argument about evolutionary dynamics.

claim: Slower gain and loss makes further coadaptation at additional genes more likely.
source: The difficulty of evolving the trait de novo is likely to slow down the rate at which it is gained and loss, which in turn makes further coadaptation at additional genes more likely.
evidence: This is a theoretical argument about evolutionary dynamics.

claim: IG14 contains 4 genes annotated as being phage related and a further 19 hypothetical proteins.
source: In our data, one example is IG14 which contains 4 genes annotated as being phage related and a further 19 hypothetical proteins (Figure 6).
evidence: This describes the composition of IG14 shown in Figure 6.

claim: 56% of the 469 strains had none of the 23 genes in IG14.
source: 56% of the 469 strains had none of the 23 genes, while 36% had more than 12 of them and 8% had between 1 and 5, which presumably represent remnants of an old phage infection.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about the distribution of IG14 genes.

claim: 36% of strains had more than 12 of the IG14 genes.
source: 56% of the 469 strains had none of the 23 genes, while 36% had more than 12 of them and 8% had between 1 and 5, which presumably represent remnants of an old phage infection.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about the distribution of IG14 genes.

claim: 8% of strains had between 1 and 5 IG14 genes, which presumably represent remnants of an old phage infection.
source: 56% of the 469 strains had none of the 23 genes, while 36% had more than 12 of them and 8% had between 1 and 5, which presumably represent remnants of an old phage infection.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding with an interpretation about phage remnants.

claim: Only one gene (VP1563) in IG14 was found in appreciable frequency in strains that had none of the other genes.
source: Only one gene (VP1563) in IG14 was found in appreciable frequency in strains that had none of the other genes.
evidence: This is a finding about the distribution of a specific gene in IG14.

claim: VP1563 might represent cargo of the phage infection that is able to persist for extended periods in the absence of infection due to a useful biological function.
source: This gene might represent cargo of the phage infection that is able to persist for extended periods in the absence of infection due to a useful biological function of its own.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the persistence of VP1563.

claim: VP1563 might additionally be transmitted by other mechanisms besides phage.
source: Alternatively, it might additionally be transmitted by other mechanisms.
evidence: This is an alternative speculative explanation for VP1563 distribution.

claim: In IG3, all strains either have the gene yniC or at least 4 out of a set of 5 genes VP0363-VP0367.
source: For example, in IG3 (Figure 6), all of the 469 strains either have the gene yniC, which is annotated as being a phosphorylated carbohydrates phosphatase, or at least 4 out of a set of 5 genes VP0363-VP0367 that includes a phosphotransferase and a dehydrogenase in the same genome location.
evidence: This describes the incompatibility pattern in IG3 shown in Figure 6.

claim: Only one strain has both yniC and VP0363-VP0367 genes.
source: Only one strain has both sets of genes.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about the incompatibility in IG3.

claim: In IG42, there are three genes that are mutually incompatible.
source: Another pattern is found in IG42 (Figure 6), where there are three genes (polar flagellar sheath protein and hypothetical proteins) that are mutually incompatible in our data
evidence: This describes the incompatibility pattern in IG42 shown in Figure 6.

claim: 12% of strains have none of the three incompatible genes in IG42.
source: and 12% strains have none of the three genes.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about IG42.

claim: At a stringent cutoff of 10-2.2, SuperDCA identifies the same multi-locus interactions as Fisher exact test does at P < 10-10, with a few SNPs excluded.
source: At a stringent cutoff of 10-2.2, SuperDCA identifies the same multi-locus interactions as Fisher exact test does at P < 10-10, with a few SNPs excluded (Figure 7b).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparison of methods shown in Figure 7b.

claim: The significance thresholds for both Fisher exact test and SuperDCA could be relaxed to identify a substantially larger number of true-positive hits.
source: The significance thresholds for both the Fisher exact test and SuperDCA could be relaxed to identify a substantially larger number of true-positive hits, at the likely expense of some false ones, but we do not investigate these associations further here.
evidence: This is a statement about potential methodological adjustments.

claim: Totally 1,103 global V. parahaemolyticus genomes were used in this work.
source: Totally 1,103 global V. parahaemolyticus genomes were used in this work, which also were analyzed in our other study (Yang et al., 2019a).
evidence: This describes the dataset used, with citation to Yang et al., 2019a.

claim: Totally 565,466 bi-allelic SNPs were identified in 198 VppAsia genomes.
source: Totally 565,466 bi-allelic SNPs were identified and 151,957 bi-allelic SNPs with minor allele frequency >2% were used in coadaptation detection.

source: Totally 565,466 bi-allelic SNPs were identified and 151,957 bi-allelic SNPs with minor allele frequency >2% were used in coadaptation detection.

source: Totally 46 Vibrio genomes revealed above than 60% coverage on lateral flagella region in V. parahaemolyticus genome and was used in phylogeny rebuilding.

source: In total 3,000 SNPs were identified in this region and were used for NJ tree construction.
evidence: This describes the SNPs used for phylogenetic analysis of lateral flagella.

claim: Totally 11 strains were randomly selected from four EGs for phenotype experiments.
source: In the phenotype experiments, totally 11 strains were randomly selected respectively from four EGs that defined by IG1 variants, including 4 EG1a strains (B1_1, B3_1, B5_3, C3_10), 1 EG1b strain (B1_10), 2 EG1c strains (C5_2, C6_5) and 4 EG1d strains (B1_3, B2_10, B4_8, C1_5).
evidence: This describes the strains used for phenotypic experiments.

claim: Five clones for each strain were used in motility assays.
source: Five clones for each strain were cultured overnight at 30°C and then inoculated in the swimming plate (LB media containing 0.3% agar) and swarming plate (LB agar with 3% NaCl).
evidence: This describes the experimental design for motility assays.

claim: Five replicates were performed for each strain in biofilm formation assays.
source: In panel a-c, five replicates were performed for each strain
evidence: This describes the experimental design for phenotypic assays.
